stemBlocks.value: Make x the subject of the formula y = x + 9.
Think first: x is nearly alone already — only the +9 has to be removed.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p095-q01 from workbook page 95.

solutionSteps.instruction: Turn the equation round so the new subject is on the left.

contentBlocks.value: An equation reads the same either way

strategyBlocks.value: Undo the addition by subtracting 9 from both sides, then write x on the left.

whyThisWorks.value: A formula is a balanced equation, so whatever you do to one side you must do to the other. Subtracting 9 is the inverse of adding 9, which strips the +9 away and leaves x standing alone without changing the relationship between x and y.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing x = y + 9 by copying the sign instead of inverting it.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing x = y + 9 by copying the sign instead of inverting it.
Avoid this: Subtracting 9 from only one side.

commonErrors.misconception: Leaving the answer as y − 9 = x without stating it as x = …
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Leaving the answer as y − 9 = x without stating it as x = …

examTip.value: Always finish by writing the new subject on the left with an equals sign — examiners want to see the formula in the requested form.
